name: Cano mac Gartnáin

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cano mac Gartnáin is an Irish hero. He stands close to the man Cáel. Both of them are warrior poets. Each one loved Créd, the princess of Connacht. Créd was the daughter of king Guaire. Cano fled to Ireland after the killing of his father. Créd was already wife to a king. Still, they fell in love without delay. Cano put off their joining. He waited until he won back his own kingdom. He then gave his outside soul to Créd. The soul took the shape of a stone. They planned a secret meeting. Meanwhile the stepson of Créd threw the plan aside. He was the child of her old husband. In despair Créd killed herself. In her fall she crushed the stone. The blow also ended the life of Cano.

okr.objective: Cano mac Gartnáin is a hero whose soul stayed outside his body.
key_results: Cano is an Irish hero of warrior-poet clan.
